provenance: Official Solana Foundation transaction-v1-examples at commit baa8b2654d1695d62c17dd8a0d2ef775ef45ad14; fixture generated with @solana/kit 8.4.0
discoveries: For legacy/v0 transactions, priority fees are charged from requested compute-unit limit times CU price, not actual consumed compute; overspecified CU limits cost money.
Official docs and examples describe active V1 messages with the 0x81 prefix; configuration carries total priority fee and resource limits, and ComputeBudget instructions do not configure V1.
Duplicate instructions of the same compute-budget variant cause transaction failure for legacy/v0 processing; execution budget also has a 1.4M CU cap.
patterns: distinguish requested CU limit from consumed units
derive fee estimate from exact message/runtime version and reconcile to finalized meta.fee
sources.overlap: Veritas now bounded-parses the V1 header, config mask, inline addresses, and instruction boundaries. It exposes priorityFeeLamports, computeUnitLimit, loadedAccountsDataSizeLimit, and requestedHeapSize for diagnostics. All V1 instructions remain UNKNOWN and complete is always false, so SigningFirewall rejects the message as TRANSACTION_DECODER_INCOMPLETE. Canonical transaction meta.fee remains realized-fee authority.
risks: V1 output is diagnostic only: instruction semantics, address authorization, and signature binding are not complete, so signing remains rejected.
The message priority-fee config is not the realized total transaction fee; base/signature fees and finalized meta.fee reconciliation remain outside this decoder.
The custom parser has bounded structural validation but is not a Solana runtime validator; protocol-version semantic checks and adversarial review remain required.
validation: Use an official SDK-generated V1 wire fixture and compare all decoded config fields and message identities.
Exercise malformed masks, truncated fields, invalid account/program indexes, trailing bytes, and size bounds.
Keep every V1 result incomplete and prove SigningFirewall rejects it; do not enable V1 signing without independent protocol/security review and complete effects/signature binding.
Compare message estimates to confirmed meta.fee including failed transactions; canonical fee remains authoritative.

provenance: Local Truth-X and execution economics source review
discoveries: The documented network fee is base signature fee plus prioritization fee, and is charged whether a transaction succeeds or fails.
Base fee counts transaction signatures and supported precompile signatures; priority fee formula rounds micro-lamports up, while v1 stores an absolute total priority fee in the message.
Jito tips and venue/protocol fees are separate economic components; net outcome accounting should not collapse them into one network-fee field.
patterns: store observed total fee and version-specific fee components separately
keep tips and venue fees distinct
sources.overlap: Truth-X captures raw transaction `meta.fee`; execution economics exposes base/priority/tip components; paper simulator uses independent configured values. EconomicDeltaEngine now derives base fee as observed total fee minus an explicitly observed priority fee and rejects a reported burned component larger than that base fee. A missing priority-fee observation leaves the base-fee component unknown. The separate Version 1 signing-wire decoder and end-to-end reconciliation across failed trades, tips and venue fees remain incomplete. A new cross-venue paper-accounting patch models one 5,000-lamport signature base fee in addition to priority fee and Jito tip for filled simulated transactions in CommandGateway, the terminal reducer/bridge, and the paper adapter; rejected pre-landing attempts do not receive this assumed base fee. This is a fixed one-signature simulation assumption, not version-aware finalized fee reconciliation. The Veritas V1 decoder now exposes the message-declared total priority fee as a diagnostic field, but does not infer base/signature fees or claim that field equals realized meta.fee; fee reconciliation remains open.
risks: estimated fee and realized network fee can diverge
unsuccessful transactions still incur network fees
fee schema may not represent future transaction versions
validation: test feeBurnedLamports <= feeLamports - priorityFeeLamports when both components are present
keep base fee unknown when priority fee is absent
fixture success and failure fees, signature/precompile counts, v0 and v1 fee models
regress different transaction fee payer vs observed wallet and preserve gross delta
reconcile separate Jito tip transfers and venue fees to account deltas
prove all-in net PnL has no double count or omission

focused regression covers buy cost basis, sell realized PnL, gateway fee report, and terminal fee display; engine build and terminal production build passed; actual finalized meta.fee reconciliation and multisignature/version-aware fee decomposition remain open
V1 message fee config is diagnostic only; verify actual total fees using confirmed transaction metadata for successful and failed transactions.

discoveries: Solana publishes production checks across RPC usage, transactions, operations and monitoring; a reachable endpoint or successful build is not a production-readiness result. SYLPH's current recorded operational blockers include stale/overflowed Core feed, stale RPC evidence, duplicate legacy Terminal processes and unavailable configured adapters.

The project has an explicit Start SYLPH check and read-only live status audit, but existing listeners predate some source-level ownership fixes, so checkout state and running-process state must be reported separately.

The declared package manager is pnpm 11.19.0, but the checked-in pnpm lock omitted two direct package dependencies; the worktree node_modules junction also resolved Pump SDK 4.0.0 despite the project pinning 2.0.0, so a pinned scratch install was needed to establish build evidence.
patterns: turn checklist items into observable gates
keep freshness, capacity, recovery and incident evidence distinct
fail closed on unknown runtime schema
sources.overlap: Current launcher check reports blockers and does not claim live readiness. Prior read-only observation found Engine PAPER/feed blocked and old Terminal processes; this batch did not start, stop or restart any service. A scratch clean install exposed stale pnpm/package-lock files and an external node_modules junction whose Pump SDK version does not match the declared pin. Both lockfiles were reconciled in the candidate branch; a pinned scratch install and engine build were then verified.
risks: new source code does not update already running processes
connectivity can be mistaken for durable capacity or chain completeness
a broad checklist can give false assurance without evidence binding
the user worktree's junction remains unmodified and local runtime modules may still differ from the lock until reinstalled
validation: run a clean install using each documented package manager against its frozen/locked file
build with exact pinned dependencies rather than a shared node_modules junction
bind process identity, source build ID and status schema
